implementation_notes: Keep `private readonly List<Contact> _contacts = new();` and publish either `IReadOnlyList<Contact> Contacts => _contacts;` (a compile-time read-only interface, .NET 4.5) or `_contacts.AsReadOnly()`, which the BCL documents as 'a read-only wrapper around the current List<T>' that reflects later changes to the list but exposes no mutators. Membership changes go through AddContact/RemoveContact. This is the cheap default because the wrapper/allocation happens once, but callers see a live view.
pitfalls: ReadOnlyCollection<T>/IReadOnlyList<T> are live views: enumerating one while the owner mutates the list throws InvalidOperationException ('Collection was modified'), so callers that iterate concurrently need a snapshot.
A `readonly List<T>` field protects the reference, not the contents - the list is still mutable through the field and it is not encapsulation.
The wrapper throws NotSupportedException only at run time; publishing IReadOnlyList<T> moves the guarantee to compile time, which is why it reads better in the public signature.

variants.name: ImmutableList<T> / ImmutableArray<T> snapshot (System.Collections.Immutable)
variants.implementation_notes: Replace the mutable list with ImmutableList<T> (or ImmutableArray<T>): Add/Remove return a new collection and the original is unchanged, so the property can hand out its current value with no wrapper and no defensive copy - what a reader receives can never be mutated later. Oracle-style trade-off in the BCL docs: 'When you add or remove items from an immutable list, a copy of the original list is made with the items added or removed'. Choose it when readers must be isolated (threads, UI bindings, cached projections); the live wrapper above remains the right call when the collection is large and mutated often.
pitfalls: Every update allocates a new list (structurally shared, but still a fresh root): a tight add/remove loop is measurably more expensive than List<T>.Add - measure before switching wholesale.
ImmutableList<T> implements IReadOnlyList<T>, not a mutable IList<T>: interop APIs that demand List<T>/IList<T> force a ToList() copy at the boundary.
A public property with `private set` still exposes a setter to the containing class only - do not widen it to `internal set` or the mutation path leaves the owner.
